title: Narrative is the recurrent tipping point for editorial drift — target it first
description: Across the available experimental runs, the Narrative stage is the most frequent first observable location where a company-first editorial hierarchy breaks, making it the highest-leverage place to test upstream-boundary controls and targeted fixes.
audience: Product/content leads, experiment designers, prompt engineers, editorial QA
rationale: Why it matters: The report localizes the earliest visible hierarchy shift most often to Narrative (multiple runs across Experiments 007–009). Focusing corrective trials at the Narrative stage lets teams test whether preserving upstream subject selection (company-first + product-as-support) is sufficient to prevent downstream reframing, or whether earlier stages must also be constrained. Gaps and uncertainty: The finding is observational, not causal — some runs show Idea or Synthesis-origin drift (e.g., Experiment 008 Idea-driven runs and Experiment 007 candidate 003 with Synthesis drift). The evidence set is limited to the archived runs and a single reconstructed brief hash; a controlled trial is required to confirm where the most effective intervention sits.
evidence: Fact: 'Narrative is the most recurrent first visible hierarchy shift in the available records.' Examples: Experiment 007 candidate runs 001–002 show first visible break in Narrative; Experiment 008 A-002 and Experiment 009 baseline 002/003 and candidates 001–003 also list Narrative as the first clear shift. Counterexamples noted: Experiment 007 candidate 003 shifted at Synthesis; several Experiment 008 B (technical-first) runs intentionally start technical at Idea. Interpretation: The report treats 'first drift' as the earliest observable stage that departs from the requested company-first hierarchy; it does not assign model-level causation.
